title: Neutrinos left the Sun's core 8 minutes ago. Sunlight's energy, tens of thousands of years ago
description:
Two things from the Sun's core reach Earth. Neutrinos made in fusion fly straight out of the Sun in about two seconds and arrive about eight minutes later; tens of billions cross every square centimetre of you each second. The energy takes the slow road: absorbed and given off again over and over, then carried up by churning gas, it leaves the surface as sunlight tens of thousands of years later, maybe far more. The Borexino detector in Italy counted the neutrinos from fusion's first step, about 140 a day in every 100 tonnes of its liquid. In 2014 that count matched what the sunlight predicts to within about 10%, so the core is burning about as hard now as when today's sunlight set out.
